title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 21
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: 63 is 18% of what number?
questions.explanation: If 63 is 18% of a number, that number is 63 / 0.18 = 350. Checking: 18% of 350 is 63. Taking 18% of 63 instead gives 11.34, which shrinks the figure when the question calls for it to grow.

questions.prompt: If 2x + 3y = 31 and 4x − y = 27, what is the value of y?
questions.explanation: Multiplying the second equation by 3 gives 12x − 3y = 81. Adding it to the first eliminates y: 14x = 112, so x = 8. Substituting back into 2x + 3y = 31 gives 16 + 3y = 31 and y = 5. 8 is the value of x, which is the step before the answer.

questions.prompt: Eight numbers have a mean of 25. One of them, 14, is then doubled. What is the new mean?
questions.explanation: The eight total 200. Doubling 14 adds another 14 to that total, making 214 over the same eight numbers: 26.75. Doubling the mean itself gives 50 and would be right only if every number had been doubled.

questions.prompt: A chord of a circle of radius 13 cm lies 5 cm from the centre. How long is the chord?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, making a right-angled triangle with sides 5, half the chord, and 13. Half the chord is the square root of 13² − 5² = 144, which is 12, so the chord is 24 cm. 12 cm is only half of it.

questions.prompt: Two cars cover the same distance, and their speeds are in the ratio 5 : 6. What is the ratio of the times they take?
questions.explanation: Over a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed, so the ratio of times is the ratio of speeds reversed: 6 : 5. The faster car takes less time, so writing the times in the same order as the speeds, 5 : 6, has the slower car finishing first.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest integer greater than the square root of 150?
questions.explanation: 12² is 144, which is below 150, and 13² is 169, which is above it. So the square root of 150 lies between 12 and 13, and 13 is the smallest integer above it. 12 is the largest integer below.

questions.prompt: A fair coin is tossed and a fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of a head together with a score above 4?
questions.explanation: A head has probability 1/2, and a score above 4 means a 5 or a 6, which is 2/6 or 1/3. The two are independent, so the chance of both is 1/2 × 1/3 = 1/6. 1/3 is the die on its own, and adding the two probabilities rather than multiplying them would give a figure larger than either.

questions.prompt: A shop offers "buy 3, get 1 free". What single discount is that equivalent to?
questions.explanation: The customer takes 4 items away and pays for 3, so one item in every 4 is free — a discount of 25% on what would otherwise be paid. Reading the free item against the 3 paid for gives 33.33%, which measures against the wrong total.

questions.prompt: 20 workers can finish a job in 18 days. After 6 days, 5 of them leave. How many days does the whole job take?
questions.explanation: The job is 20 × 18 = 360 worker-days. The first 6 days use 120 of them, leaving 240 for the 15 who stay: 16 more days. The whole job therefore takes 6 + 16 = 22 days. 16 days counts only the second stretch.

questions.prompt: Someone walks 9 km due north and then 12 km due east. How far are they from where they started?
questions.explanation: The two legs are at right angles, so the direct distance is the square root of 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225, which is 15 km. 21 km is how far they walked, not how far they finished from the start.

questions.prompt: Taking pi as 3.14, the period of a pendulum is 2 pi times the square root of L divided by g. What is the period when L = 0.9 and g = 10?
questions.explanation: L divided by g is 0.09, and its square root is 0.3. Multiplying by 2 × 3.14 = 6.28 gives 1.88. Skipping the square root gives 0.57, a tenth of the size, because the root of a number below 1 is larger than the number itself.

questions.prompt: How many days are there from 12 March to 5 May, counting 5 May but not 12 March?
questions.explanation: March has 31 days, so 19 remain after the 12th. April adds 30 and May adds 5, giving 19 + 30 + 5 = 54 days. Counting the starting day as well gives 55, which is the usual source of a one-day error in date arithmetic.

questions.prompt: A recipe for 4 portions uses 300 g of flour and 5 eggs. With 800 g of flour and 12 eggs, how many whole portions can be made?
questions.explanation: Each portion needs 75 g of flour and 1.25 eggs. The flour would stretch to 10.67 portions, but the eggs run out at 9.6, so 9 whole portions can be made. Going by the flour alone gives 10 and ignores that the eggs are the binding constraint.

questions.prompt: An agent earns 6% commission and is paid £1,530.00. What were the sales?
questions.explanation: Commission of £1,530.00 at 6% means sales of £1,530.00 / 0.06 = £25,500.00. Checking: 6% of £25,500.00 is £1,530.00. Taking 6% of the commission gives £91.80, which runs the calculation the wrong way round.

questions.prompt: Six values are 15, 18, 21, 23, 27, 31. A seventh value of 40 is added. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: With six values the median was the average of the third and fourth, (21 + 23) / 2 = 22. With seven it is simply the fourth, which is 23. Adding a value above all the others pushes the middle position up one place, so the median rises from 22 to 23 even though nothing near the middle changed.

questions.prompt: Two circles have radii in the ratio 3 : 5. The larger has an area of 100π cm². What is the area of the smaller?
questions.explanation: Areas of similar figures scale as the square of the radius ratio, so the areas are in the ratio 9 : 25. That makes the smaller 100π × 9/25 = 36π cm². Scaling by the radii themselves gives 60π cm².

questions.prompt: 6 machines make 4,200 units in 5 days. At the same rate, how many units do 8 machines make in 3 days?
questions.explanation: 6 machines over 5 days is 30 machine-days for 4,200 units, so one machine-day makes 140. 8 machines over 3 days is 24 machine-days: 3,360 units. Scaling by the machines alone gives 5,600 and leaves the shorter run out of it.

questions.prompt: One seventh written as a decimal repeats the block 142857 for ever after the decimal point. What is the 100th digit after the point?
questions.explanation: The block 142857 repeats every 6 digits. 100 divided by 6 leaves a remainder of 4, so the 100th digit is the 4th of the block: 8. A remainder of zero would mean the last digit of the block, 7, which is the case worth checking separately.

questions.prompt: Fixed costs are £4,800.00 and each of 300 units costs £22.00 to make. At what price must each unit sell to break even?
questions.explanation: The fixed costs come to £16.00 a unit across 300 units, on top of the £22.00 each one costs to make: £38.00. Selling at £22.00 would cover the making but none of the £4,800.00 of fixed costs.

questions.prompt: If x + 1/x = 5, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
questions.explanation: Squaring both sides gives (x + 1/x)² = x² + 2 + 1/x² = 25, since x × 1/x is 1 and the middle term is twice that. Taking the 2 across leaves x² + 1/x² = 25 − 2 = 23. Squaring without allowing for the middle term gives 25.

questions.prompt: A bureau sells euros at 1.18 to the pound and buys them back at 1.28 to the pound. If £400.00 is changed into euros and immediately changed back, how much is lost?
questions.explanation: £400.00 buys 472 euros. Changing those back at 1.28 gives 472 / 1.28 = £368.75, so £31.25 has gone in the spread. Multiplying the 0.1 gap by the £400.00 gives £40.00, which treats the spread as if it applied to pounds rather than to euros.
